transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?
I've been hearing voices lately that nobody else can hear, and it's really terrifying. I also just feel so incredibly depressed and completely unmotivated, and it's been like this for months now.
Have the voices ever happened for at least 2 weeks when you were not feeling depressed or having other mood symptoms?

Yes, actually. There was a period a few months ago for about three weeks where my mood felt completely fine and I wasn't feeling down at all, but I was still hearing those voices. It really scared me because I thought they would go away when I started feeling better, but they didn't.

During the times you’ve had voices, have your depression symptoms been present for most of the illness overall, or have there also been long periods when the voices were there but you were not depressed?

Overall, the depression has definitely been present for most of the time I've been dealing with this. But there was that specific period of about two or three weeks where I was still hearing the voices even though I didn't feel depressed at all.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Schizophrenia, Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)], but the patient reports a clear period of at least 2 weeks with auditory hallucinations in the absence of mood symptoms, while depressive symptoms have been present for most of the illness overall. This pattern fits schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, and makes schizophrenia less likely because mood symptoms are not absent throughout the illness.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent depressive symptoms for most of the illness plus auditory hallucinations, and importantly reports at least 2–3 weeks of hallucinations occurring while mood symptoms were absent. This meets the key criterion for schizoaffective disorder and argues against major depressive disorder with psychotic features, where psychosis occurs only during mood episodes.
